land.text: the Nile 'from the 3rd cataract to south of Abu Hamed at Mograt Island', the Makurian core after Kush's collapse

predecessors.note: The page: Kush was 'collapsing' by the early 4th century, Nubians settled the valley in the 4th century and 'a new Makurian state emerged by the 5th century' (infobox 'Established: 5th century'). 347 is Cliopatria's hand-over from its Kush row (ends 346).

land.text: Lower Nubia, ruled from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim after the loss of Dongola in 1365: the kingdom as it stood in 1414

successors.note: Hand-over to the same state, not a succession: Cliopatria's 'Makuria Kingdom' row (1415-1518, slug makuria-kingdom, same Wikidata Q829356) is this kingdom's last century (Nazir dethroned 1397, Joel attested 1463, 'Makuria collapsed soon after Joel, probably in the late 15th century'). One colour for both slugs (rule 2); the makuria-kingdom dossier is written by another part of group af-01 and should open with a found event written as a hand-over.

capitals.name: Dongola (Old Dongola)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Dongola (5th century to 1365)'; the city was founded in the late 5th century (c. 500), so the dot stands at the site from the dossier's start although no seat is attested before c. 500. Coordinates from the project gazetteer (places.jsonl 'Old Dongola').

capitals.name: Gebel Adda
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gebel Adda (after 1365)': 'In 1365, a civil war ended with the loss of Dongola. The court moved to Gebel Adda.' The page gives no coordinates; these are the researcher's for the site on the east bank opposite Abu Simbel, now under Lake Nasser (gazetteer name needed).

keyframe_review.note: 347-568, 65,260 km2: the Dongola reach 'from the 3rd cataract to south of Abu Hamed at Mograt Island', which is the page's 'initial extent'. Unverified start: the page dates the state to the 5th century and Cliopatria to 347 (its Kush row ends 346); kept as drawn with the found event at confidence 1. The infobox gives no area figure to compare.
569-622: no border move. The keyframe year matches John of Biclar's record (c. 568) that Makuria had 'received the faith of Christ'; a delegation reached Constantinople in 573.

correction.text: as drawn until 640; from 641 with Nobatia, which Makuria annexed 'likely during the 620s, before 642', after which Makuria 'extended north to Philae'

keyframe_review.note: 623-655: Cliopatria keeps Nobatia separate until 655 and merges it in 656, but the page puts the annexation before 642 (a bishopric founded at Faras c. 630) and the Second Battle of Dongola page has 'northern and central Nubia ... united under the Makurian king Qalidurut' in 652. The ledger's 641 merge (confidence 1) carries the change; the nobatia dossier ends in 641 to match.

656-681, 212,627 km2: Makuria with Nobatia, north to Philae/Aswan. Right in shape, fifteen years late in date (see makuria_623). The Baqt of 652 fixed the relationship with Egypt but the pages name no border point.
682-691: differs from its neighbours by 54 km2, a drawing artefact; no event on the pages opened.

692-849: the Baqt era. Kyriakos's raid on Upper Egypt c. 747 and the flight of Marwan II's sons to Nubia in 750 moved no border; the Baqt lapsed in the 830s (Fourth Fitna) and was renegotiated in 835 (payment every three years).

850-1110: the kingdom's peak 'between the 9th and 11th centuries'. The raids on Upper Egypt of 951 (Kharga), 956 (Aswan) and 962-964 (as far as Akhmim) are in the ledger as a two-year occupation, not a border change.

correction.text: the shape unchanged; Qasr Ibrim hatched as Ayyubid-occupied from January 1173 to 1175, and the whole kingdom in the vassal tint from 4 June 1276, when the Mamluks installed Mashkouda, after the Mamluk army sent out on 20 January 1276 had defeated Makuria at Dongola

keyframe_review.note: 1111-1278: a status change only. The Mamluk client relation (puppet kings Mashkouda 1276, Simamon by 1286) belongs to the mamluk-sultanate dossier as vassal_start 1276; it is flagged in notes so the me-09 agent records it.

correction.text: the kingdom unchanged under Mamluk-installed kings (Mashkouda from 4 June 1276, Simamon by 1286, Mamluk invasions in the late 1280s): a Mamluk client in the vassal tint, not Mamluk territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Makuria shape for 1279-1293 and draws the land as Mamluk Sultanate (its Alodia row borders the Mamluks in those years). The page records no annexation: the kings kept their throne at Dongola between invasions, so the state continues.

correction.text: as drawn; Dongola and the south are lost in 1365 (ledger), leaving Lower Nubia ruled from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim, after 'a civil war ended with the loss of Dongola' and Dongola 'was captured by the tribesmen and its king killed' (Banu Kanz page); a Mamluk client in the vassal tint until then (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 1294-1406: Cliopatria keeps the Dongola reach in Makuria to 1414 (and in 'Makuria Kingdom' to 1518). The spec is the shape at 1294; the 1365 loss of Dongola and everything south of Lower Nubia is the ledger event of 1365 (Makuria page: 'Due to a civil war in 1365, the kingdom was reduced to a rump state that lost much of its southern territories, including Dongola'), as makuria_1407 already gives Lower Nubia only. Muslim kings from 1316 (Barshanbu; a mosque in the throne hall attested 1317) change nothing territorially.

correction.text: Lower Nubia only, from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim to the Egyptian frontier; Dongola had been lost in 1365

keyframe_review.note: 1407-1414: the Banu Kanz 'were expelled from Aswan in 1412/3'; Nazir had been dethroned in 1397. The row hands over to makuria-kingdom (same state) in 1415.

region.text: the Nile 'from the 3rd cataract to south of Abu Hamed at Mograt Island'

ledger.note: 347: Makuria rises on the Dongola reach after Kush's collapse. The page: Kush was 'collapsing' by the early 4th century, 'a new Makurian state emerged by the 5th century', Dongola founded in the late 5th century; the year is Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush, not the page's. Old Dongola page (read 2026-10-18 for the thin item): 'Old Dongola was founded in the fifth century as a fortress' and 'in the mid-sixth century with the arrival of Christianity it became the capital of Makuria'; it gives no founding year for the kingdom, so 347 stays Cliopatria's hand-over from Kush at confidence 1.

region.text: Nobatia, from the third cataract to Philae: Makuria 'then extended north to Philae'

ledger.note: 641: Makuria absorbs Nobatia. The annexation was 'likely during the 620s, before 642' (a bishopric founded at Faras c. 630); the Nobatia page: 'The merger most likely occurred before the Muslim conquest in 652', at the latest 'By 707'; the Second Battle of Dongola page: in 652 'northern and central Nubia were united under the Makurian king Qalidurut'. 641 is the latest year consistent with 'before 642'; the nobatia dossier ends here. Faras page (read 2026-10-18): says only that 'When Nobatia was absorbed into Makuria, it remained the most prominent center in the north' and gives no year, so 641 stays the latest year that fits the Makuria page's 'before 642' (confidence 1).

region.text: Upper Egypt from Aswan 'as far as Akhmim'

ledger.note: 962: Makurian forces hold Upper Egypt as far as Akhmim. The page lists raids on Upper Egypt in 951 (Kharga Oasis), five years later (Aswan) and '962-964 (as far as Akhmim)'; the three-year span is drawn as an occupation (hatched), not a border change. Egypt was under the Ikhshidid governors, whom Cliopatria draws as Abbasid; the counterpart is Cliopatria's row.

region.text: Upper Egypt from Aswan to Akhmim

ledger.note: 964: the Makurians withdraw from Upper Egypt; Egypt fell to the Fatimids in 969 and Ibn Salim al-Aswani visited Georgios III 'immediately afterward'.

region.text: Qasr Ibrim, taken by Turan-Shah in January 1173

ledger.note: January 1173: Turan-Shah takes Qasr Ibrim. After Makurian forces 'pillaged Aswan' in 1172, Saladin's brother took the fortress; 'Kurdish raids lasted two years'. Hatched Ayyubid occupation of Makurian land (rule 4); the owner records it here, the ayyubid-sultanate dossier with the roles reversed. Routing: Cliopatria's rows are Fatimid Caliphate 911..1176 and Ayyubid Sultanate 1177..1249, so Egypt in 1173-1175 is the fatimid-caliphate row; the ayyubid-sultanate counterpart is kept, and me-09 must either start the Ayyubid dossier by 1173 (Turan-Shah, Saladin's brother) or carry the reverse event under fatimid-caliphate.

region.text: Qasr Ibrim and the Lower Nubian valley to Adindan

ledger.note: 1175: the Ayyubid raids end 'in 1175 at Adindan' and Qasr Ibrim returns to Makuria.

minus.text: Maris, the Nubian reach south of Aswan, which the Banu Kanz "migrated south to occupy"; the gazetteer's Lower Nubia (Aswan to the Second Cataract) without the Aswan district
everything south of 22.9 N: Qasr Ibrim, Gebel Adda, Adindan and Faras, which the Makuria page keeps Makurian

region.text: Maris, the 'northern Nubia' that the Banu Kanz 'migrated south to occupy': the Aswan side of Lower Nubia (north of 22.9 N) without the Aswan district; Qasr Ibrim, Gebel Adda and the Adindan reach stay Makurian

ledger.note: After 1174 (bridged to 1175): the Aswan side of Lower Nubia (Maris) passes to the Banu Kanz, mirror of banu-kanz ledger 2. Banu Kanz page, opened 2026-11-01: 'the Banu Kanz migrated south to occupy Maris' ('northern Nubia'); the page gives no year and no extent. This page (opened 2026-11-01) never uses the name Maris and keeps Qasr Ibrim ('in 1175 a Nubian army finally arrived to confront the invaders at Adindan near Faras'), Gebel Adda and Adindan Makurian, so only the strip north of 22.9 N (21 cells) goes. Added fx-25.

region.text: the whole kingdom, 'turning Makuria into a Mamluk vassal state'; the Dongola reach and Lower Nubia stay Makurian

ledger.note: 4 June 1276: 'Mashkouda was installed on the Makurian throne on 4 June 1276', after the Mamluks 'dispatched a large army on 20 January 1276' that 'met the Nubian army at Dongola, defeating it decisively'; the king 'had to swear an oath of fealty to Baybars, thus turning Makuria into a Mamluk vassal state' and 'was forced to send regular tribute in addition to the Baqt, transfer Lower Nubia to Baybars', 'although the latter conditions were probably never put into action'. So the kingdom stays whole in the vassal tint (rule 4), not Mamluk land; Mashkouda was assassinated soon after and Simamon held power by 1286. The mamluk-sultanate dossier carries the mirror vassal_start with counterpart makuria.

1316: Abdallah Barshanbu, the first Muslim king of Makuria, is installed by the Mamluks; he 'was slain in late 1317' and 'a mosque in the throne hall was attested in 1317'. The state and its name continue (rule 2): a caption-only event marking the change of dynasty and religion at Dongola; Kudanbes had usurped the throne in 1311, the Kanz al-Dawla seized it after 1317 (Banu Kanz page).

region.text: Dongola and the Nile valley south of Lower Nubia: 'In 1365, a civil war ended with the loss of Dongola'; Dongola 'was captured by the tribesmen and its king killed' (Banu Kanz page)

ledger.note: 1365: Dongola falls in the civil war; the court flees to Gebel Adda. The Banu Kanz page: the Banu Kanz and Banu Ikrima 'then controlled the area from Aydhab and Suakin west to the Nile'; the Kanz al-Dawla and other chiefs surrendered to the Mamluk governor of Qus in December 1365 and the Mamluks 'returned to Egypt in early 1366'. The region is the researcher's reading (everything outside Lower Nubia); banu-kanz needs a dossier (notes).

region.text: the kingdom as it stood before the civil war of 1365

ledger.note: 1365: bridging a silence. The Makuria page gives no date for the end of Mamluk suzerainty; it has the 1365 civil war reduce the kingdom to 'a rump state', and the Mamluk expedition that 'returned to Egypt right after, in early 1366' without reconquering Dongola. The Baqt page says the treaty 'finally came to an end in the mid-fourteenth century' with 'the complete collapse of organized government in the region' (Baqt page). 1365 is the researcher's bridge, not a page date.

1365: the court moves to Gebel Adda in Lower Nubia (infobox 'Gebel Adda (after 1365)'); Mamluk letters of 1367 went to Apakyre at Gebel Adda and to Shihab al-Din Majid at Qasr Ibrim. Old Dongola page (read 2026-10-18): 'The royal court left Dongola in 1364' - one year earlier than the Makuria page; 1365 kept as the Makuria page's year.

region.text: Lower Nubia, ruled from Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim

ledger.note: 1414: Cliopatria's 'Makuria' row ends and its 'Makuria Kingdom' row begins; the pages describe one continuous kingdom (Nazir dethroned 1397, the Banu Kanz expelled from Aswan 1412/3, Joel attested 1463, collapse 'probably in the late 15th century'), so this is a hand-over to the same state under a second slug, with one colour (rule 2). The year is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: First Battle of Dongola
wars.outcome: Makurian victory: Uqba ibn Nafi's column of 20,000 horsemen reached Dongola, 'were beaten back, and Amr withdrew from Nubia'; no territorial change.
wars.note: Infobox date 'Summer' 642; the page lists Nobatia separately among the Christian kingdoms but names Makuria as the opponent at Dongola.

wars.name: Second Battle of Dongola
wars.outcome: Makurian victory: Abdallah ibn Sa'd 'laid siege to the city' with about 5,000 men and a catapult, suffered heavy losses and 'called off the siege in exchange for a pact', the Baqt (360 slaves a year against wheat, barley, wine, horses and linen), which 'reportedly lasted six centuries'.
wars.note: The Baqt page: mutual non-aggression, free trade, no settlement in the other's land, extradition, a mosque at Dongola; it 'names no border point'. Empty zones: no cell changed owner.

wars.name: Makurian raids on Upper Egypt
wars.outcome: Raids on Kharga (951) and Aswan (956); in 962-964 Makurian forces reached Akhmim. No annexation; the ledger draws 962-964 as an occupation.
wars.note: Egypt's rulers were the Ikhshidids (Cliopatria: Abbasid). Kyriakos's earlier raid c. 747 (Umayyad Egypt) is on the same page and held no ground.

wars.name: Ayyubid invasion of Nubia
wars.outcome: Makurian pillage of Aswan in 1172; Turan-Shah took Qasr Ibrim in January 1173; 'Kurdish raids lasted two years, ending in 1175 at Adindan'. No permanent change.

wars.name: Mamluk–Makurian wars

zones.text: Dongola, taken in 1276 and in the late 1280s

wars.outcome: Mamluk raid to Dongola 1265; David sacked Aidhab 1272; the Mamluk army sent out on 20 January 1276 defeated Makuria at Dongola, and the Mamluks installed Mashkouda on 4 June 1276; Simamon held power by 1286 and Mamluk invasions followed in the late 1280s. Makuria became a Mamluk client (vassal tint from 1276) without annexation.
wars.note: Cliopatria removes Makuria for 1279-1293 and draws the land Mamluk; the new keyframe makuria_1279 keeps it as a client state.

wars.name: Mamluk interventions and the Muslim kings
wars.outcome: Kudanbes usurped the throne in 1311; the Mamluks installed Barshanbu in 1316 (slain late 1317); the Kanz al-Dawla, arrested in Cairo and released, 'seized the Makurian throne' and two Mamluk expeditions against him failed, 'the last in 1324' (Banu Kanz page); Siti reigned 1328-1333.

wars.name: Makurian civil war and the fall of Dongola

zones.text: the Dongola reach, lost to the tribesmen

wars.outcome: Dongola 'captured by the tribesmen and its king killed'; the court moved to Gebel Adda; a Mamluk expedition took the surrender of the Kanz al-Dawla at Qus in December 1365 and the Mamluks returned to Egypt early in 1366. Makuria survives in Lower Nubia.
wars.note: The Makuria page dates the civil war's end and the loss of Dongola to 1365; the Banu Kanz page dates the capture to the reign of al-Ashraf Sha'ban without a year.

certainty.note: Every frontier approximate: the cataracts (third, then first) are the only fixed points; the Alodian frontier near Abu Hamed/al-Abwab is a reading of the pages.

The Egyptian frontier at Aswan/Philae is fixed in effect by the Baqt of 652, though the pages name no border point; the desert and Alodian frontiers stay soft; after 1365 the southern limit (Batn el-Hajar) is the researcher's.

notes:
Rows and slugs. Cliopatria's 'Makuria' (347-1414) and 'Makuria Kingdom' (1415-1518) share Wikidata Q829356 and the pages describe one continuous kingdom (Dongola lost 1365, court at Gebel Adda, Nazir 1397, Joel 1463, collapse late 15th century, 'Around 1500, John the Syrian reported Nubians had no king'); they are one state. The orchestrator assigned makuria-kingdom to another part of group af-01, so this dossier reviews only the 'Makuria' shapes and hands over to makuria-kingdom in 1414 as the same state (one colour, rule 2), like the eastern-roman-empire to byzantine-empire hand-over. If the orchestrator prefers, merge the two rows under 'makuria' with both Names in cliopatria_names. The 'Makuria Kingdom' 1507-1518 shapes (240,898 km2, reaching 17.3 N) are larger than any Makurian extent after 1365 and look wrong; the makuria-kingdom agent should check them. Dotawo is the Old Nubian name of Makuria on the page, not a separate state.

Nobatia. Cliopatria merges Nobatia into Makuria in 656; the Makuria page puts the annexation 'likely during the 620s, before 642', the Nobatia page 'most likely before 652', 'By 707' at the latest. This dossier dates the merge 641 (confidence 1) and the nobatia dossier ends 641; the First Battle of Dongola (642) and Second (652) pages have the Arabs fighting Makuria at Dongola.

Cliopatria gap 1279-1293: no Makuria shape; the land is drawn Mamluk. The new keyframe makuria_1279 keeps the kingdom as a Mamluk client. The mamluk-sultanate dossier (me-09) should carry vassal_start 1276 (Mashkouda installed 4 June 1276) for makuria and an end when the relation lapsed (the page gives no date; the Baqt 'ended in the mid-fourteenth century'), plus the hatched occupations of Dongola during the invasions of 1276 and the late 1280s if its pages date them. The ayyubid-sultanate dossier should carry the Qasr Ibrim occupation January 1173-1175 with roles reversed.

Repair of 2026-10-18 (reviewer): makuria_1294 is now the shape at 1294 and the 1365 loss is the ledger event; vassal_start 1276 (June) and vassal_end 1365 (confidence 1) added for the Mamluk client status, so the mamluk-sultanate dossier needs the mirror vassal_start 1276 and vassal_end 1365 (counterpart makuria); the 'Dongola, taken 20 January 1276' wording is corrected (20 January 1276 is the day the army was sent out); the Qasr Ibrim occupation of 1173-1175 names ayyubid-sultanate, but Cliopatria's Fatimid row runs to 1176 and the Ayyubid row starts 1177, so me-09 must start the Ayyubid dossier by 1173 or the reverse event goes under fatimid-caliphate.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Banu Kanz (banu-kanz; Aswan principality from 943, Kanz al-Dawla title 1006, in Maris after 1174, Dongola 1365, dissolution 1365 per its infobox but the Kunuz continued), the Ikhshidids of Egypt if Cliopatria has no row (the 951-964 raids are recorded against abbasid-caliphate, Cliopatria's owner of Egypt then).

Gazetteer names needed: Qasr Ibrim (place, 22.65 N 31.99 E, given as a coordinate), Gebel Adda (place), Faras/Pachoras (place), Batn el-Hajar and al-Maris (regions of Lower Nubia), Abu Hamad (place), Dongola reach (region: the Nile between the third cataract and Abu Hamad).

Pages silent: the Baqt page and both Dongola pages name no border point; no page gives an area figure; the Makuria page does not date the Banu Kanz capture of Dongola beyond 1365 or the end of Mamluk suzerainty. fx-25 (2026-11-01): mirror loss of the 21-cell Aswan side of Lower Nubia (Maris) to banu-kanz in 1175; the rest of Lower Nubia stays Makurian.
